posts.author: John Klayer
posts.content_md: I had a great weekend. I set up a canopy tent at a caving event in north Georgia this past weekend to display some of my cave holograms. By one estimate, over 200 people came by to ooh and aah. Gosh, it felt good!

posts.author: Jem
posts.content_md:
Hi John

That's sounds great, it must have been a good feeling 

Is there any chance of posting a couple of pictures of your cave holograms, i'd love to see them. I used to be into caving and potholing a few years ago, sadly, my health now limits my adventures. I can't think of anything better than combining two great hobbies 

Cheers

Jem

posts.author: rzeheb
posts.content_md: Hi John. What fun! I've been caving (off and on) for about 30 years. It seems to me that the best caves, that I can more or less conveniently reach, are mostly in your neck of the woods. I try to get down to West Virginia for a long weekend of caving maybe once every 2 or 3 years; it's a 12 or 14 hour drive down from the Boston area. It must have been quite difficult to lug your equipment safely into the cave and then set up and shoot holos with all the mist and humidity.

posts.author: Jem
posts.content_md:
Whoa... Nice 

Thanks for the links Dave 

John, that limestone 'hole' sure looks tempting , brings back many happy memories. Here's a couple of my favourites in the Yorkshire Dales, England.

[http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s1_bFMSqieQ](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s1_bFMSqieQ)

[http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k_Mg9aLv ... re=related](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k_Mg9aLv6bQ&feature=related)

The first link is Swinsto hole, to say that it's a little 'wet' is an understatement. The second is Gaping Ghyll, one of our larger caves, the winch is erected twice a year by the local potholing clubs to make access a little easier 

None of the folks in the videos are known to me, but they were nice clips, so I thought i'd post the links .

Cheers

Jem

posts.author: BobH
posts.content_md: Great work John! I can't think of many projects in home holography that beat yours for appropriateness. Bringing poorly accessable scenes from out of the dark into the light of day. what an excellent use of the "window with a memory" aspect of holography. Displaying them as laser lit transmission holograms is absolutely the way to go! Thanks for doing it, and sharing your results here.

posts.author: John Klayer
posts.content_md: The videos were interesting Jem. Do a google search on Flowing Stone to see what my friends Tom Moltz, Scott Carmine and myself are proud to have discovered a few years ago. Heck yeah rzeheb, the good ones are in my neck of the woods - Georgia has the best caves in the world! Are you in the NSS? BobH, I agree laser transmission holos are great. They have the most depth and can capture so much. I'm working on trying to improve the fiber reference process.

posts.author: Jem
posts.content_md:
Wow John... You were really involved in discovering that cave , that must have been one hell of a feeling 

Our caves in the Yorkshire Dales can't live up to some of the caves you have out there, but we do have a few that have some very special formations.

All the best.

Jem

posts.author: John Klayer
posts.content_md: Yeah, discovering that cave was a great thrill sort of like making my first hologram.
